dedupe_keys.name: evacpath r package for road constrained least cost pedestrian evacuation modelling tsunami and other hazards

description: evacpath is an R package for estimating how long it takes people to walk out of a hazard zone along the road network. It was published on CRAN in May 2026 by Elvin Cordero, whose maintainer address is at the University of Puerto Rico, and builds on a 2025 paper by Cordero and colleagues and on the leastcostpath package of Joseph Lewis. Functions prepare hazard zones, generate evacuation origin points along roads, identify escape or safety points, build a conductance surface from slope, compute the least-cost distance to safety and convert it into evacuation-time polygons. Helpers designed for tsunamis handle land-only hazard zones, zones combined with water and road-aware escape boundaries, and the package is meant to be adaptable to other regions and hazards. Version 0.1.0 is free to install from CRAN under the MIT licence, with vignettes for applying it to a new region. Caveats: it is a first release, it models walking time, not crowd interaction or congestion, and results depend on the hazard zone and elevation data supplied. Coverage is general. Simulation uses: mapping evacuation times and places people cannot reach in time, to plan shelters, vertical evacuation and warning. Related records: the Berkeley disaster evacuation surveys (data-berkeley-disaster-evacuation-surveys) give behavioural data on evacuation.
name: evacpath: R package for road-constrained, least-cost pedestrian evacuation modelling (tsunami and other hazards)
